text:
Alyssa: heads-up — we saw sustained RSS growth on cfg-x when INT8 quant is enabled and we feed long chats (~64k tokens). baseline fp16 stays flat. wondering if this is a kv-slot fragmentation issue or something in the int8 page reuse path.
Diego: can you paste the trace? do we have perf-tool outputs?
Alyssa: short dump from a repro VM:
```
rss_before=11.8G
rss_after=15.2G (after ~1200 tokens)
kv_pages_alloc=3240
kv_pages_free_list=68
int8_frag_ratio=0.47
```
not huge alloc churn but free_list is tiny. free pages exist but not reused for new slots (they end up allocating new pages).
Matt: fwiw kernel selection switched to the packed-int8 GEMM set last week (#PR 1824). could be alignment/padding differences causing per-slot footprint changes.
Sara: batching heuristics changed too — we started more aggressive micro-batching for latency. fewer tokens per batch -> smaller contiguous writes to KV. might increase fragmentation.
Elaine: rolling hypothesis: int8 quant reduces per-key size but our slot allocator expects fixed chunk sizes tuned for bf16/fp16. with smaller records we now create more tiny fragments and metadata overhead dominates; compacting is lazy so memory grows.
Alyssa: experiments: revert kernel selection to fp16-compatible path on one node, and also flip batching heuristics to previous config. both nodes ran the long-context loader for 2h. results: fp16 path node stayed ~12G RSS, int8 node jumped to 15G and kept climbing. batching revert lowered growth rate but didn't eliminate it.
Diego: that points to allocator + quant interplay. do we have telemetry for per-slot size distribution?
Alyssa: added a quick profiler:
```
slot_size_hist = {64: 4200, 128: 1900, 256: 320, 512: 48}
avg_metadata_per_slot=24 bytes
page_size=4096
```
most slots tiny, lots of internal fragmentation.
Matt: note: int8 implementation pads keys to 64 bytes for vectorization alignment on some kernels. if slot data < pad we waste that padding. combined with metadata overhead we get >1x worse than theoretical.
Sara: also saw more frequent cache-eviction churn in logs: older slots get evicted, then re-created soon after because micro-batches request slightly different context windows. that causes double churn.
Elaine: actionable list: 1) add per-slot compaction when free_list falls under threshold, 2) adjust pad strategy for int8 kernels (only pad when necessary or use compact kernels), 3) tweak batching to prefer larger contiguous token runs when longctx mode is on.
Alyssa: did a quick A/B of compacting every 10k tokens; RSS stabilizes ~13G but p50 latency increases by ~6ms for some requests. cost vs latency tradeoff.
Diego: we should quantify accuracy delta for int8 vs fp16 on our eval prompts too. there was a small regression reported by SRE on chat-quality when int8 was enabled for this model.
Matt: I ran an eval: int8 topo + old pad -> rouge drop ~0.9% on targeted QA prompts. switching to compact kernel reduces drop to ~0.3%. fp16 baseline is 0.0.
Sara: telemetry idea: track (slot_reuse_rate, avg_slot_hole_size, eviction_rate) per model variant and annotate traces with kernel id + batching policy. if reuse_rate < 0.6 for >5min trigger compaction.
Elaine: agree. we should also add a kernel-selection safeguard: if model is longctx-heavy and quant==int8, prefer compact kernel set even if slightly slower. we can add cost function: effective_memory_saving = baseline_mem - measured_mem_post_compact - latency_penalty_cost.
Alyssa: can someone pick up a quick patch to allocator compaction? propose small PR: when free_list < 128 and hole_ratio > 0.25 run compaction pass that merges adjacent free slots and reclaims pages. minimal API change.
Diego: I can take the allocator compaction patch. will add unit tests + perf microbenchmark.
Matt: I'll look into kernel padding flags and add a runtime toggle per node to switch to compact int8 kernels.
Sara: I'll tune batching heuristics for longctx mode and add a canary test in dedicated region.
Elaine: I'll own the eval runs and define the acceptance thresholds (latency + quality). propose: quality degradation <=0.5% absolute and p50 latency penalty <=5ms for rollout.
Alyssa: thanks. timeline: Diego/PR by EOD Thu, Matt kernel toggle in next 48h, Sara canary after that. Elaine will run evals after compaction patch.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: alloc-compact-v1 -> canary pool at 2026-03-20T04:00Z (rolling). :robot_face:
Matt: quick note — add a debug flag to log slot allocation decision for 1% of requests so we can validate heuristics without full perf hit.
Diego: good call. will include.
Alyssa: great. if anyone finds a simpler immediate mitigation: increasing the free_list watermark reduced growth in testing by ~30% with zero latency impact (temporary knob). we can flip that until patches land.
Sara: I'll flip watermark on canary nodes and watch. :eyes:
Alyssa: appreciate it. will follow up with a short postmortem once we have numbers. :thumbsup:
